correctness.rationale: An explicit base-b carry computation realizes exactly all adjacent residue pairs satisfying c-a≡1 mod gcd(b-1,m). The block recurrence gives exact 3/4-factor families and short counts. Any length-4 factor crosses at most one base-b block boundary for b>=3 and thus has at least two +1 increments; its reversal would have at least two -1 increments, impossible for m>=3. No distinct reverse triple is possible; the gcd-based length-two reversal orbit formula follows by directly checking the pair congruence. Symbolic verification across 104 parameter pairs and separate direct prefixes support the algebra. Factor complexity for long lengths is accurately attributed to Starosta.

value.rationale: The b>=3 theorem answers a natural multi-base variant of the published Question 62 with a structural local-to-global rigidity proof; the gcd(b-1,m) trichotomy is a meaningful arithmetic phase transition distinguishing periodic and aperiodic languages and gives exact small reflection spectra. The b=2 previously known claim does not subsume the result. This is an all-parameter language classification, not arbitrary finite enumeration.
